sponsor_or_proposer: Botswana Power Corporation (BPC) / Government of Botswana (plant owner)
current_state: BPC/government is procuring to fuel the existing 2x45MW (90MW) dual-fuel OCGT plant at Orapa (currently diesel) with either LNG or coal bed methane. An owner's-engineer tender was issued to develop 'LNG and coal bed methane gas infrastructure' to supply the plant (per African Energy); an earlier BPC tender (ref 4765-20, 'Supply and Delivery of Natural Gas to Orapa 90MW Power Plant', 2021) also exists. BPC's generation GM stated in 2022 'We are thinking of importing LNG to fuel the 90MW.'
missing_threshold_elements: Facility type is undetermined: the procurement explicitly weighs an LNG path against a coal-bed-methane (pipeline-fed) path, so it is not yet established that any LNG receiving/storage/regasification facility (a trucked/virtual-pipeline LNG satellite station, since Botswana is landlocked) will be built rather than a CBM-pipeline gas supply with no LNG terminal. No confirmed LNG storage/regas scope, no capacity for an LNG facility, no FID, no awarded EPC/operator for an LNG facility. Sponsor (BPC) and location (Orapa) are clear; the concrete step is procurement-stage, but it does not yet commit to an LNG facility specifically.
watch_for: Award of the owner's-engineer / gas-infrastructure contract specifying the LNG path; a tender or contract for an LNG satellite/regas/storage station or truck-LNG receiving terminal at Orapa; selection of LNG over CBM-by-pipeline; any FID, capacity (m3 storage / regas mtpa), or LNG supplier (e.g. trucked from Botala Serowe or imported via South Africa/Mozambique). If the LNG path is selected and a receiving facility is scoped, graduate to a new_terminal (import/satellite) with BPC/Govt of Botswana as owner (run entity_lookup first).
notes: DISTINCT from the existing GEM 'Botswana LNG Terminal' (T100001048162, Botala Energy, Serowe export/liquefaction): different sponsor (BPC/Govt vs Botala), different location (Orapa, ~200km from Serowe), and import/fuel-supply side rather than export. Tlou Energy's Lesedi CBM project was also checked and is gas-TO-POWER only (no LNG/liquefaction) -> excluded (see qa). Both lead URLs verified via url_verifier.py (PASS). Corroborating lead: https://www.mmegi.bw/business/bpc-to-replace-diesel-with-lng-at-orapa-plant/news . Re-check ~6-12 months. Note: a CBM-only outcome would not be an LNG terminal at all.
